title.narrative: Inclusive Growth in Mozambique Phase III (2025-2028)
Inkluderande tillväxt i Mocambique Fas III (2025-2028)

description.narrative: IGM is a research and capacity development programme implemented by the National Directorate of Economic and Development Policies (DNPED) of the Ministry of Planning and Development of Mozambique (MPD) and the Centre for Economic and Management Studies (CEEG) of the Faculty of Economics of the Eduardo Mondlane University (UEM), in partnership with the United Nations University World Institute for Development Economics Research (UNU-WIDER). The overarching aim of the programme is to enhance the Mozambican government’s capabilities and policy processes to address economic policy challenges over the short-, medium- and long-term. This phase III will focus on developing local capacity and producing evidence to support improved macroeconomic management, pro-poor public revenue and spending, and development of concrete policy options to raise the wellbeing of the poorest through sustained and inclusive economic growth.

IGM är ett forsknings- och kapacitetsutvecklingsprogram som genomförs av det nationella direktoratet för ekonomisk och utvecklingspolitik (DNPED) vid Moçambiques ministerium för planering och utveckling (MPD) och Centre for Economic and Management Studies (CEEG) vid Eduardo Mondlane University (UEM), i samarbete med United Nations University World Institute for Development Economics Research (UNU-WIDER). Det övergripande syftet med programmet är att förbättra den moçambikiska regeringens kapacitet och politiska processer för att hantera ekonomiska politiska utmaningar på kort, medellång och lång sikt. Denna fas III kommer att fokusera på att utveckla lokal kapacitet och ta fram bevis för att stödja förbättrad makroekonomisk förvaltning, offentliga inkomster och utgifter för de fattiga, och utveckling av konkreta politiska alternativ för att öka välbefinnandet för de fattigaste genom hållbar och inkluderande ekonomisk tillväxt.

The overarching aim of Phase III of the IGM programme (2025-2027) is to enhance the Mozambican governments capabilities and policy processes to address the economic policy challenges over the short, medium and long-term. Phase III will focus on developing local capacity and producing evidence to support improved macroeconomic management, pro-poor public revenue and spending, and development of concrete policy options to raise the well being of the poorest through sustained and inclusive economic growth. IGM will maintain its critical support to the Government of Mozambique to adopt stronger evidence-based economic policies, but also with emphasis on medium- and long-term strategic thinking and planning, which will contribute to broader-based sustainable development.
The specific objectives of IGM Phase III are to:
1) Produce rigorous evidence to address key policy challenges and inform Mozambiques development strategy over the next decades (evidence generation).
2) Develop research and analytical capabilities at MPD, as well as in local academia, to support stronger evidence-based policy (capacity development).
3) Stimulate policy uptake, engaging key policymakers across multiple fora to drive policy debate and evidence-informed decision-making (policy engagement & communication).
These objectives will be reached by focusing on three thematic areas; Poverty Inequality and social protection; Macroeconomics; and Public Finance. The two cross-cutting themes concerning economic policy challenges of preparing for and adapting to Climate Change, and considerations about Gender Inclusiveness in economic policy will be explicitly addressed in all areas of work.

description.narrative:
Examples of results during 2025
Output 1 - Policy-relevant research studies
- IGMs social protection work in 2025 built on the 2024 Vulnerable Lives Survey to assess trade-offs in programme design, particularly the effectiveness of targeting under operational and fiscal constraints. The research contributed to policy dialogue with government and partners and supported evidence-based discussions at the IGM Annual Conference 2025.
- IGMs work within education focused on analysing school-to-work transitions through a follow up survey of university and TVET graduates, providing insights into employment outcomes, job quality, and gender dynamics, in close collaboration with the Ministry of Labour to ensure policy relevance.
- IGM initiated exploratory work to strengthen access to public expenditure and revenue data through engagement with the Ministry of Finance, laying the groundwork for a future budget and execution data set, although no consolidated data set was produced during the reporting period.
- IGMs climate change work in 2025 focused on defining its analytical agenda and developing the FORÇA project (support to the Climate directorate) but broader progress was limited due to programme reprioritisation and staff reallocation. As a result, no major analytical outputs, including the planned Green Paper, were produced during the reporting period. Due to Sweden's phasing out, the FORÇA project was not realised under the Sida support.
- Analytical work in late 2025 focused on in depth studies using IOF2022 data while laying the groundwork for future poverty analysis based on IOF2025.
- Macroeconomic work in 2025 focused on maintaining key data sets and launching the first CEEG Economic Bulletin to strengthen accessible analysis of economic trends, while planned training activities were cancelled due to time and resource constraints. In parallel, discussions on macroeconomic tools were slowed by institutional changes, though targeted technical support was provided on issues such as mobile money taxation and short term GDP forecasting.
Output 2) Training and capacity development
In 2025, short term training under IGM primarily focused on aligning and developing the training curriculum with the Phase III research agenda, resulting in limited delivery of trainings such as Microsoft Office and an initial course on poverty measurement, while most other planned trainings were postponed to 2026 to ensure coherence with revised programme priorities.
The National Resident Advisor (NRA) scheme was developed as a key innovation to strengthen sustainability and create career pathways for Mozambican researchers, with extensive preparatory work undertaken in 2025 including recruitment processes in collaboration with key partners. However, due to the need to reprioritise Phase III activities within a reduced time frame and budget, the scheme was ultimately discontinued before recruitment could be finalised.
The IGM traineeship scheme aims to build analytical capacity among young Mozambican economists, but the planned recruitment of a new cohort in 2025 was deferred to 2026 due to the need to reprioritise Phase III activities and budget constraints.
The program initially included a long term training component aimed at building national expertise through scholarships for advanced studies. However, in 2025 this element was discontinued due to a shortened implementation period and high costs that no longer aligned with the revised budget. An exception was made for one participant whose studies had already begun prior to the revision and are expected to conclude in 2026. No new long term training commitments were initiated during the reporting period.
In 2025, technical assistance continued to support key partner institutions by strengthening the use of existing analytical tools, data sets, and methodologies, particularly in macroeconomic planning and poverty analysis. The work built on capacities developed in earlier phases, contributing to policy processes and ensuring continuity despite program adjustments. Support focused on improving data use and methodological approaches rather than introducing new large-scale systems, while also reinforcing research capacity and ongoing data collection efforts within academic and government institutions.
Output 3 Policy engagement and communications
The focus was on launching Phase III, promoting strategic outreach and collaboration, and establishing a foundation for continued research uptake and evidence based policy dialogue.
During the reporting period, several research outputs were produced, including two working papers and one peer reviewed journal article, covering topics such as political economy, social protection, and post disaster support. In addition, a new flagship economic bulletin was launched with two editions, strengthening policy relevant macroeconomic analysis and information access. While a blog post was also published, the production of shorter communication products was limited due to the transition to a new programme phase and prioritisation of major activities.
Online communication and dissemination remained a central pillar of IGMs outreach strategy during the second half of 2025, supporting the visibility, accessibility, and uptake of programme outputs among national and international audiences. The IGM programme continued to actively use its website, social media channels (Facebook, X, and LinkedIn), and the IGM Update newsletter to disseminate analytical outputs and event-related information.
Outreach activities during the reporting period focused on launching Phase III and promoting its analytical priorities through high level events and stakeholder engagement, while also aligning partners through a planning retreat. Efforts were concentrated on flagship events that positioned the programme within national policy discussions and strengthened its role as a bridge between research and policy.
The CEEG seminar series continued to provide a platform for academic exchange at the Faculty of Economics, with five seminars held during the period covering a range of policy relevant research topics and supporting a stronger research culture.
